title: AgentDescent: a parallel, asynchronous framework for self-evolving LLM agents
description:
AgentDescent puts the distributed deep-learning training stack on top of agent self-evolution. The "parameters" are a library of evolvable artifacts (skills, prompts, harness modules, verifiers); the "gradients" are diffs carrying evidence cards; and the "optimizer step" is a merge decision. N workers propose diffs in parallel and a barrier-free asynchronous aggregator merges them into a shared, version-controlled artifact library.

The one place the analogy must break defines the system: gradients add and diffs do not, so aggregation is not averaging but conflict resolution, fusion, statistical acceptance and transactional commit. When an artifact is held in a single key every concurrent pair conflicts and merge-of-N degenerates into best-of-N selection at best-of-N validation cost. Reflective merge — a model asked to write the union of the contradicting proposals, gated by the same acceptance test as any other candidate — is what removes that degeneracy.

Nineteen published self-evolution algorithms (among them ACE, GEPA, ADAS, DGM, OpenEvolve, ERA, Voyager, Reflexion, PromptBreeder and AFlow) run as plug-ins over eight named policy slots, under serial, synchronous and barrier-free schedulers, without modifying the engine. The core engine has no required dependencies and needs only Python 3.9 or later.

Accompanying paper: AgentDescent: Asynchronous Parallel Self-Evolution of LLM Agents by Merging Conflicting Edits.
